body.statement:
If the characteristic function \(\chi\) of a probability law on \(\mathbb R\) is integrable, then that law has a bounded continuous density
\[
 f(x)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-itx}\chi(t)\,dt.
\]

source.locator: Characteristic Functions, second edition, Section 3.3, inversion theorem
source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 3.2.2. If a characteristic function f(t) is absolutely integrable over (−∞,+∞), then the corresponding distribution function F(x) is absolutely continuous and the formula p(x) = (1/2π) ∫ e^(−itx) f(t) dt expresses its density function p(x) in terms of the characteristic function. The density function p(x) is continuous.

attestation.note: Verified against the accessible scan of Lukacs, Characteristic Functions, 2nd ed., pp. 33–34. The exact direct result is Theorem 3.2.2; the frozen locator saying Section 3.3 is imprecise (Section 3.3 later gives a generalized inversion corollary). The attested theorem exactly supports the node.
